newsitem.title: USA: New Haven seeks economic growth through arts.
newsitem.headline: New Haven seeks economic growth through arts.

text.p: New Haven intends to push cultural tourism and the arts to promote economic development, city officials said Thursday.
They told a news conference that the second annual International Festival of Arts and Ideas will be held June 25-29 of next year.
This year's event - billed as one of the biggest festivals of its kind in New England - attracted 60,000 people and pumped $5.16 million into the city's economy during five days in June, they said.
The city of 120,000 has suffered from falling property values and a depressed retail sector in recent years. Among the major setbacks was the 1993 closing of Macy's department store.

"In trying to pull people back into supporting and appreciating the downtown core, I think the arts is the way to go," Matthew Nemerson, president of the Greater New Haven Chamber of Commerce, told Reuters.
He said the local economy will be further bolstered by the September 1997 opening of the $20-million Omni Hotel, which will have 270 guest rooms and a conference center.
